recommendations.reason: He would rather have no wine than one wine for the whole menu, so he defers to his wine club friends, guessing pinotage with the braai.
recommendations.quote: I'd love to know what they paired with South African Clairebit.
recommendations.speaker: Pierre Novellie

recommendations.item: Coconut cream cake
recommendations.reason: He had a giant, moist, entirely coconut slice on his first holiday with his partner and still thinks about it all the time.
recommendations.quote: it was just one of the best things I've ever had.
recommendations.speaker: Pierre Novellie

recommendations.item: Sichuan food (cucumber, chicken feet)
recommendations.reason: He loves its Sichuan cooking, located next to Arsenal's stadium.
recommendations.quote: I'm missing out how much I love Sichuan things. Xi'an Impression next to Arsenal Stadium.
recommendations.speaker: Pierre Novellie

episodes.title: Melvin Odoom
episodes.summary: Melvin Odoom's menu: his mum's Perrier with lime, Honey & Smoke sourdough, Nando's olives and Skewd halloumi, his mum's spicy jollof, Palm Bay macaroni pie, Supermalt, and hot apple pie with cold ice cream.

recommendations.item: Perrier sparkling water with a twist of lime
recommendations.reason: His mum's special bottle of Perrier that he used to sneak sips of as a kid; sparkling feels like a treat.
recommendations.quote: Mum's Perrier water with a twist of lime would be my go-to.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Sourdough ball with butter
recommendations.reason: A friend's Turkish Cypriot-leaning Mediterranean grill that bakes a massive sourdough ball with amazing butter; he sometimes just orders that as his starter.
recommendations.quote: they do the best sourdough bread there. It's like this massive ball, comes with the most amazing butter.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Olives (with garlic and mushrooms)
recommendations.reason: Thinks Nando's olives are the pinnacle of olives, and Ed and James agree on the green-heavy ratio.
recommendations.quote: I just think it is the pinnacle of olives.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Grilled halloumi, nicely tanned, thin and crispy
recommendations.reason: A Mediterranean place near Cockfosters with what he thinks is the best halloumi: browned, crispy, thin and not squishy.
recommendations.quote: they do like the best halloumi.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Mum's Ghanaian jollof rice with spicy chicken
recommendations.reason: His mum's cooking is his number one, and the jollof must be properly spicy; she only taught him the recipe because of MasterChef.
recommendations.quote: Mum's jollof rice with chicken, spicy chicken.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Macaroni pie (Caribbean mac pie)
recommendations.reason: A West Indian spot whose Bajan-style macaroni pie he loves enough to drive halfway to meet the Deliveroo rider.
recommendations.quote: there's a little place called Palm Bay, little West Indian in Essex. And they do the best
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Supermalt
recommendations.reason: A malt drink that is a staple of Ghanaian family parties; it must be drunk cold. He brought bottles for the hosts.
recommendations.quote: that's how you test a good party, if they got Supermalt.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Hot apple pie or flambeed apple tart with cold ice cream
recommendations.reason: He loves the hot and cold combination and favours The Ivy's flambeed apple tart with ice cream on the side.
recommendations.quote: I love a hot and cold combination.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Dining in the dark
recommendations.reason: Used to be his go-to date restaurant, where blind waiters serve you in total darkness; he is not sure it is still open.
recommendations.quote: for years it used to be my go-to... It's where you dine in the dark.
recommendations.speaker: Melvin Odoom

recommendations.item: Chamomile and honey halloumi, tasting menu
recommendations.reason: James and Ed recommend this vegetarian Middle Eastern restaurant for its melty honey halloumi and tasting menu.
recommendations.quote: Bubala has really good halloumi. They do this like chamomile and honey halloumi
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

recommendations.item: Jollof rice boxes
recommendations.reason: Ed mentions the street food place with huge portions where he used to eat the whole box.
recommendations.quote: there's a street food place called 'Jollof Mama', and yeah, the boxes are absolutely huge.
recommendations.speaker: Ed Gamble

episodes.title: Paul F. Tompkins (Tasting Menu)
episodes.summary: A Tasting Menu episode: Paul F. Tompkins is served Alex Horne's chaotic dream menu (Orangina, Mighty White with shrimp Primula and a Pop-Tart, pork scratchings, penne with pesto and frankfurters, Christmas dinner, spicy communion wafers, a moules-and-bread-sauce-and-Baileys drink, a Mars bar) and reacts with distaste; his own original picks included still water, cream soup, a cold Amstel and New York cheesecake.

recommendations.item: Orangina (Alex Horne's pick); Paul's own: still water
recommendations.reason: Alex swapped water for the fun-bottle orange fizzy drink; Paul thought orange to start a meal was odd but recalled it as a novelty in the US, and mused about Liquid Death instead.
recommendations.quote: I remember when it was a new thing in the states. It was a fun bottle. It was an exciting time.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: Mighty White medium-sliced bread with butter, shrimp Primula, sliced cheese, plain gluten and a Biscoff Pop-Tart (Alex Horne's)
recommendations.reason: A deliberately silly bread course; Paul found the shrimp cheese-in-a-tube combo bleak and wouldn't open a meal with a Pop-Tart.
recommendations.quote: No, this is bleak.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: Crisp platter with dips, pork crackling and one hairless pork scratching (Alex Horne's); Paul's own: cream soup
recommendations.reason: Paul eats pork crackling but only a few pieces; the hosts explain pork scratchings as pub bar snacks.
recommendations.quote: I like it okay. A little bit goes a long way.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: Penne with pesto, Boursin, frankfurter and cheddar; a Jamie Oliver pork roll; Christmas turkey with trimmings (Alex Horne's)
recommendations.reason: A kid-style pasta with three cheeses; Paul liked the cheese count but thought chopped hot dogs belong in mac and cheese; the pork roll is from a Jamie Oliver-branded place.
recommendations.quote: The concept of the cut up hot dogs, I think works with like a macaroni and cheese... But not in a pasta.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: Spicy communion wafers (Alex Horne's)
recommendations.reason: Paul correctly guessed this joke side; he found real hosts terrible but loved the ceremony and incense of Catholic Mass.
recommendations.quote: It was terrible... it's supposed to be bland. It's unleavened bread.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: Moules mariniere juice with bread sauce and a glug of Baileys, in a pewter tankard (Alex Horne's); Paul's own: a pint of cold Amstel
recommendations.reason: A made-up gross mix that made Paul feel sick; he prefers a cold Amstel and enjoyed Camden Hells in its branded glass.
recommendations.quote: The first ingredient is enough to make me sick.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

recommendations.item: A Mars bar (Alex Horne's); Paul's own: New York cheesecake
recommendations.reason: Alex's most honest choice; Paul likens it to a Milky Way and prefers Reese's Peanut Butter Cups.
recommendations.quote: The Mars bar, I think, is the equivalent of our Milky Way bar.
recommendations.speaker: Paul F. Tompkins

episodes.title: John Cena
episodes.summary: John Cena, mid-salmonella, picks bottled still water, Persian taftoon, a tartare, The Polo Bar's ribeye with greens and chips for his crew, a flight of espresso martini, wine and Lagavulin plus a flat white, and banoffee pie.

recommendations.item: Bottled still water
recommendations.reason: He has day-five salmonella and regrets not sticking to bottled still water.
recommendations.quote: If I had a takeback machine, bottled still.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Taftoon bread with dips
recommendations.reason: A fluffy, glazed, seeded Persian flatbread he learned to love through his wife's family, ideally from a dedicated bread place.
recommendations.quote: Taftoon is a nice, soft bread that is addicting, and there's no cutting it.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Tartare (whatever the restaurant's signature is)
recommendations.reason: He nearly always orders a tartare, fish or meat, and loves table-side preparation.
recommendations.quote: I tend to always go with like a tartare.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Medium-rare ribeye steak
recommendations.reason: The best ribeye he has had, at a fancy-comfort-food restaurant he can't order anything else at.
recommendations.quote: Their ribeye steak, man, just crushes... I can't not honour the ribeye.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Broccolini, sauteed spinach, burnt cauliflower, Brussels sprouts and fries for the crew
recommendations.reason: Creative vegetable sides for the steak, plus chips for his friends.
recommendations.quote: I would definitely go for broccolini, and most places will put some heat on it, like some chilli flakes.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Espresso martini, red wine, Lagavulin 16 and a flat white
recommendations.reason: A flight starting with an espresso martini, then Bordeaux or Burgundy, a smoky single malt, and a flat white as nightcap.
recommendations.quote: So this is a flight. I would start out with an Espresso Martini.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Banoffee pie
recommendations.reason: Discovered via the catering crew on WWE UK tours; he calls it the best dessert he has had and shared one with his wife after his last match.
recommendations.quote: Banoffee pie: man, it is the best dessert I've ever had.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Table-side mozzarella
recommendations.reason: He loves its table-side mozzarella with wonderful tomatoes, despite being about 2000 calories.
recommendations.quote: There's a great place, my home in Tampa, Florida, called Rocca, who does a mozzarella table-side.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Steak
recommendations.reason: A specific Tampa spot he and his wife go to for steak.
recommendations.quote: If you're ever in Hyde Park, if you ever get to the states, you got to go see that place. It's great
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Breakfast
recommendations.reason: A small breakfast place attached to restaurant Hide that he and his wife like to visit before walking in Hyde Park.
recommendations.quote: I love the restaurant Hide here, and they got a small breakfast place called Hideaway.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

recommendations.item: Flat white
recommendations.reason: A true beanery he tried in London; he opted for a cheaper flat white that he found incredible.
recommendations.quote: I got like a £6 or £7 flat white, and it was incredible.
recommendations.speaker: John Cena

episodes.title: Lara Ricote
episodes.summary: Lara Ricote imagines a family-run restaurant serving sparkling water, warm focaccia, pear and gorgonzola ravioli from a Miami restaurant, steamed sea bass on caramelised fennel, crispy potatoes, gazpacho as the drink and her aunt's chocolate cookie-almond torte.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: She simply prefers sparkling and finds it delicious.
recommendations.quote: I am, of course, going for the sparkling kind, for me that's better, and I think it's delicious.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Warm focaccia
recommendations.reason: She wants warm focaccia, a bread worth more than a crumb of joy.
recommendations.quote: I would like some focaccia, please. And I'd like it to be warm.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Pear and gorgonzola ravioli with cream and a little truffle, shaped like a twisted chocolate wrapper
recommendations.location: Coral Way, Miami, Florida, USA (now closed)
recommendations.reason: A tiny family-run restaurant of chefs Romeo and Gloria from Ecuador; the dish was seared into her brain and she visited every birthday. The restaurant has closed.
recommendations.quote: I had it in a place that's closed down. But it's called Romeo's, and it's in Miami, Florida. And it used to be on Coral Way.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Steamed sea bass on caramelised fennel with butter, white wine, capers, lemon and family spice mix
recommendations.reason: A dish her father and sister cook for the family; she prefers serving fish rather than beef in a restaurant her whole family would run.
recommendations.quote: You're putting sea bass on top... You're putting a white wine. You're putting capers... That goes on top with some lemon. My God, this is delicious.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Small boiled potatoes crisped with butter, salt and family spices
recommendations.reason: Crispy outside, they pair well with the sea bass.
recommendations.quote: they've had butter on them after they've been boiled, and so they're quite crispy on the outside.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Gazpacho (served in a glass, with sparkling water)
recommendations.reason: She has become obsessed with how delicious cold gazpacho is and insists it counts as a drink.
recommendations.quote: I think that it should be gazpacho. I don't care. I don't care. I think it's right.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Torta de Gala: layered chocolate, condensed milk, Maria cookies and toasted almonds
recommendations.reason: A rich, thick family cake her aunt makes (traditionally for her older sister's birthday), served despite the aunt calling it shit.
recommendations.quote: It's so thick. The bottom is Maria cookies... it's been in our family for at least 10/15 years.
recommendations.speaker: Lara Ricote

recommendations.item: Beef Wellington
recommendations.reason: James calls it the best beef Wellington he has had; Ed later got a Wagyu beef Wellington made for him there.
recommendations.quote: That's the best beef Wellington I've ever had. Ron Gastrobar in Amsterdam.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

episodes.title: Rob Auton
episodes.summary: Rob Auton builds a nostalgic restaurant filled with sofas from his life, serving a post-Blacklock hangover glass of water, his mum's hotel bread buns, bits of his dad's carved meat, a main course of dishes from everyone he has met, devils on horseback, Scrumpy Jack and limoncello, and Lidl apple strudel with ice cream.

recommendations.item: Still water, with the thirst-quenching power of 3am after a big night
recommendations.reason: Water as good as the glass you gulp at 3am after his annual all-in meat and beer night at Blacklock with university friends.
recommendations.quote: We do that thing where it's just all in, and you have all the meat... Just piles of chops, and then loads of beers.
recommendations.speaker: Rob Auton

recommendations.item: Bread buns his mum baked for the hotel she waitressed at, with salted butter
recommendations.reason: His childhood house always smelled of the bread buns his mum made before shifts at a local hotel; he wishes he had appreciated it more.
recommendations.quote: The bread I would like is bread from the hotel that my mum used to work in... the house stinks of bread.
recommendations.speaker: hotel

recommendations.item: First slices of carved lamb, pork and turkey from his dad
recommendations.reason: As a kid his dad would cut off the nicest crispy edge while carving and hand it to him and his sister.
recommendations.quote: Whenever he was carving the meat, he'd always cut off a tiny bit, like the nicest bit, and go, 'Here you go, try that.'
recommendations.speaker: home

recommendations.item: Dishes from everyone he has met, including sweet and sour chicken from a Chinese restaurant in Crete and his granny's roast potatoes
recommendations.reason: A potluck of people from his life; the sweet and sour chicken eaten with family friends in Greece in 1996 blew his mind, and his granny's roast potatoes sit alongside.
recommendations.quote: They have the sweet and sour chicken that I tasted that night for the first time. It absolutely blew my socks off.
recommendations.speaker: restaurant

recommendations.item: Devils on horseback (dates with cheese wrapped in Parma ham)
recommendations.reason: His auntie introduced him to devils on horseback, which he loves.
recommendations.quote: My auntie introduced me to devils on horseback. You know, date stuffed with goat's cheese wrapped in parma ham.
recommendations.speaker: homemade

recommendations.item: Four cans of Scrumpy Jack after pitching his tent at Glastonbury, and plenty of limoncello
recommendations.reason: The first can after the hell of getting into and setting up at Glastonbury is a perfect relief, and limoncello tastings were a highlight of planning his wedding.
recommendations.quote: I always like to get the tent up, get everything sorted, and then have a can of Scrumpy Jack.
recommendations.speaker: other

recommendations.item: Lidl apple strudel with ice cream, plus a goodie bag of snacks
recommendations.reason: A cheap supermarket apple strudel log that got him through the pandemic, tied to a happy memory with his wife.
recommendations.quote: This is something that we got into during the pandemic, which was apple strudel from Lidl... a big log. It's like £1.50.
recommendations.speaker: Rob Auton

recommendations.item: Sausage sandwich
recommendations.reason: He had a Costa sausage sandwich just before recording and swears it is great: good bread bun, three small sausages and ketchup.
recommendations.quote: They do a sausage sandwich that might not sound like much, but it's flipping awesome.
recommendations.speaker: Rob Auton

episodes.title: Andi Osho
episodes.summary: Andi Osho, who stopped drinking alcohol, picks sparkling water, poppadoms with the dips, moi-moi from Chishuru, her cousin's jollof rice with jerk chicken, Tenderstem broccoli, a virgin Old Cuban and sticky toffee pudding.

recommendations.item: Sparkling water
recommendations.reason: Since she stopped drinking two years ago, sparkling water is the drink that works in a nice restaurant.
recommendations.quote: I stopped drinking alcohol about two years ago. So, there's not really any other drink that really works
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Whole poppadom to herself with all the dips (not lime pickle or raw onion)
recommendations.reason: She loves poppadoms and takes her own, piling the dips onto a shard; she is happy to pass the lime pickle to Ed.
recommendations.quote: when I think about poppadoms, there's only love.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Moin-moin (steamed bean pudding) with cured stout and confit yolk
recommendations.reason: A modern take on a childhood Nigerian dish, eaten at the Michelin-starred restaurant when she took her mum; it felt nostalgic yet new, like a reimagined Four Seasons.
recommendations.quote: it's a little bit of my childhood, little bit of Nigeria, but it's also, you know, it's just fine dining as well.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Jollof rice with jerk chicken and the sauce from the meat stew
recommendations.reason: Her cousin makes the best jollof rice; she skips the stewed meat because she distrusts gristle and swaps in jerk chicken, like the stalls at carnival.
recommendations.quote: my cousin, I'm going to say, makes the best jollof rice.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Tenderstem broccoli, blanched, with butter and garlic
recommendations.reason: A simple green side she loves, no cream.
recommendations.quote: a little bit of butter, maybe a bit of garlic, yum.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Virgin Old Cuban (mint, lime, syrup, bitters, non-alcoholic sparkling wine)
recommendations.reason: A cocktail she'd drink if there were a virgin version, loving how the lime and sparkling wine complement each other.
recommendations.quote: I looked up the ingredients, and I was thinking this is enough to have me start drinking again because they're delicious.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Sticky toffee pudding with plain vanilla ice cream
recommendations.reason: Her favourite pudding; vanilla ice cream only, because the pudding does the sweet work.
recommendations.quote: you just can't go wrong.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Jerk chicken
recommendations.reason: Her pick for jerk chicken: the stalls with queues at Carnival, and a street festival stall in St Lucia.
recommendations.quote: any of the stalls on Carnival in Notting Hill... the main ones where there's a queue... you can't go wrong.
recommendations.speaker: Andi Osho

recommendations.item: Free welcome cookie
recommendations.reason: James raves about the warm check-in cookie, and they joke Andi should review them.
recommendations.quote: It's got chocolate chips and nuts in it. It's warm and gooey.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

episodes.title: Sara Cox
episodes.summary: Sara Cox picks room-temperature still water, a McDonald's hash brown amuse-bouche, a bread basket (challah, garlic bread, French stick, crumpet), barbecued mackerel with scallops and bacon, Roka lamb chops, her mum's mash with cold spinach and kimchi, a non-alcoholic Italian spritz and her Jeremy Vine Bake Off cake.

recommendations.item: Room temperature still water
recommendations.reason: She likes still water at room temperature, claiming it hydrates better.
recommendations.quote: I think I will just go still... It's supposed to be like room temperature water.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Hash brown straight from the fryer (amuse-bouche)
recommendations.reason: Only McDonald's hash browns will do, eaten fresh from the fryer in the paper bag, inspired by one at a service station on the way back from Bolton.
recommendations.quote: I don't like any other hash browns... unless they're the McDonald's ones.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Challah bread with salted butter
recommendations.reason: She buys her buttery, sweet challah here and eats the back of the loaf rather than the shiny crust.
recommendations.quote: Daniels in Temple Fortune, best place to get your challah bread that I know of.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Small thin garlic bread
recommendations.reason: A local Italian that does a small, thin, buttery garlic bread about the size of a seven-inch record.
recommendations.quote: Sanzio, local Italian, does garlic bread that is really small, like a seven-inch record, quite thin, and delicious.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: French stick from a local boulangerie
recommendations.reason: The French stick is from a village boulangerie on holidays at her in-laws' place; the famous Colombe d'Or restaurant is the memory attached to those trips with friends.
recommendations.quote: get a French stick from the local boulangerie. And we'd go to the Colombe d'Or
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Half a Warburton's crumpet with salty butter
recommendations.reason: A well-toasted crumpet with plenty of salty butter, not floppy.
recommendations.quote: Half a Warburton's crumpet. It's fresh out the toaster with some salty butter, but just half.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Chiew Yim (salt and pepper) ribs
recommendations.reason: Her honourable mention for the starter: tiny, salty, crunchy pork ribs.
recommendations.quote: Lovely, tiny, little, salty, crunchy, porky delight.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Barbecued mackerel, as grilled by her Uncle Trevor
recommendations.reason: Fresh mackerel grilled on a campsite barbecue in Cornwall when she was eight is the taste she has been chasing ever since.
recommendations.quote: I have spent my life searching for that taste again.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Scallops and bacon
recommendations.reason: Sweet scallops with salty bacon served in the shell; she can never order anything else there.
recommendations.quote: every time I go, I'm like, 'I'm not going to have the scallops'... nothing is as good as that.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Chargrilled lamb chops
recommendations.reason: Thin, sweet, spicy, salty chops with Korean-style spice fresh off the griddle; her favourite thing there.
recommendations.quote: I've not found sort of lamb chops quite like there.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Mum's mashed potato
recommendations.reason: Her mum Jackie mashed it in a huge pan on the kitchen floor and Sara was the official taster.
recommendations.quote: my mum always makes the best mash
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Cold spinach with sesame dressing
recommendations.reason: A Japanese restaurant staple she finds unexpectedly incredible.
recommendations.quote: it shouldn't work... the cold spinach.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Kimchi
recommendations.reason: She didn't appreciate Korean food when modelling in Seoul at 18 but loves kimchi now.
recommendations.quote: kimchi, I didn't get it then, but I love it now.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Fever-Tree non-alcoholic Italian Spritz
recommendations.reason: Since giving up alcohol this bitter Aperol-style spritz with ice is her treat drink.
recommendations.quote: Non-alcoholic Italian Spritz... It's like an Aperol Spritz.
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Jeremy Vine penny-farthing Biscoff sponge cake with raspberries and Chantilly cream
recommendations.reason: The cake she baked on Bake Off, served with ripe raspberries and whipped cream.
recommendations.quote: I did Jeremy Vine riding a penny-farthing in a Biscoff sponge, and so I will have a slice of that
recommendations.speaker: Sara Cox

recommendations.item: Szechuan lager cocktail
recommendations.reason: James enjoyed a cocktail of lager, orange liqueur, tequila and Szechuan, made in a brewery collab.
recommendations.quote: a really nice place called Cafe Kowloon... It was delicious.
recommendations.speaker: James Acaster

episodes.title: Leo Reich
episodes.summary: A beach-wedding barbecue fantasy: tap water, Burger King chips with proper mayo, bottomless grilled octopus, harissa lamb, roast pig, ice-cold Estrella Galicia, and takeaway pad see ew with chicken satay as a savoury dessert.

recommendations.item: Tap water in a big pint glass with lots of ice (ideally the runoff from a foot tap on the beach)
recommendations.reason: He wants plain tap water, and enjoys the seasoned taste of London tap water.
recommendations.quote: Tap! Tap! Simple as that. Next question.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Burger King chips with proper mayonnaise (Hellmann's or garlic mayo from elsewhere)
recommendations.reason: He rejects the bread-or-poppadoms question and picks fast-food chips, which he finds crispier than rivals; Ed agrees they are the best. He wants the mayo from a proper jar, not Burger King's.
recommendations.quote: I want Burger King chips... They're crispier. And they're like square.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Bottomless grilled octopus with lemon, olive oil, salt, garlic and parsley
recommendations.venue: Beach fire cooked by an old Greek man (imaginary)
recommendations.reason: Part of an imagined beach wedding meal, cooked over an open fire.
recommendations.quote: I want bottomless grilled octopus, I think.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Whole grilled lamb stuffed with garlic and spices, with harissa
recommendations.reason: He wants crispy-skinned whole lamb cooked on the beach fire, inspired by Moroccan pit-roast lamb with cumin salt.
recommendations.quote: It's like stuffed with garlic and there's spices on it. It's gonna get a crispy skin going.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Roast pig (a side of roast pork) and a Camel Blue cigarette
recommendations.reason: Since the fire is going he wants a whole roast pig, with a summery cigarette to go with it.
recommendations.quote: So, I want a roast pig. I want a side of roast pork and a cigarette.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Estrella Galicia, very cold on draft in a frozen glass
recommendations.reason: A crisp Spanish lager that always tastes cold, kept coming throughout the whole meal.
recommendations.quote: Light Spanish beer, so cold frozen glass. Estrella Galicia, if possible.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich

recommendations.item: Pad see ew (sweet beef noodles) with chicken satay, in a plastic takeaway container
recommendations.reason: He has no sweet tooth and wants more savoury food after a 45-minute gap, and loves the block of noodles tipped from a sealed plastic takeaway tub.
recommendations.quote: I don't have a sweet tooth at all... I'd like a pad see ew.
recommendations.speaker: Leo Reich
